intro.text: A Thaylen bodyguard and one of King Taravangian's most trusted followers in the Diagram.

items.text: On the day Taravangian solved Fabrisan's Conundrum, Mrall had to have him locked up, because the king thought it reasonable to draft a law requiring every citizen of below-average intelligence to commit suicide for the good of Kharbranth.

Mrall went with Taravangian to Vedenar after the Veden civil war, where Taravangian gained the throne. When Szeth came to confront the king, Mrall had his guards keep Taravangian apart from the Veden soldiers so he wouldn't be linked to the Assassin in White, excusing the king as old and overcome with grief. He then took Taravangian to see the dying Highprince Valam.

Mrall moved to Urithiru with Taravangian and other key members of the Diagram. On a day of notable brilliance, he had to revise Taravangian's restrictions after Adrotagia realised the king had cheated the test, and he was disturbed to find that Taravangian had made changes to the Diagram.

When Dalinar Kholin refused to yield to Odium at the Battle of Thaylen Field, Mrall wondered whether the Diagram might be flawed, and before Taravangian's meeting with Odium he suggested drafting a change of plan.

When Taravangian left Urithiru with the coalition's forces bound for Emul, planning to betray them and be captured, Mrall wept openly, unhappy that the king was disbanding the Diagram and throwing his life away. After Taravangian explained his reasons, Mrall bid him farewell with a firm handshake and a hug.
Days before the contest of champions, Mrall was killed while protecting Taravangian's family.

appearance.text: A thick-armed Thaylen man who shaves his head and eyebrows.

personality.text: No scholar, Mrall is still a full participant in the Diagram, believing in its cause and supporting its methods to "save what they can". He speaks his mind and claims he can simply switch off his emotions, yet he is awed by the destruction the war in Jah Keved has caused.

Taravangian considers his bodyguard one of his closest and most loyal friends. Mrall is also the final judge of the king's daily capacity, deciding from daily tests and the old man's behaviour what he may do without supervision.
